info.title: Nizam API — Dashboard
info.description:
The **Nizam Dashboard API** is the surface for tenant administrators, dispatchers, and operations staff working inside a single Organization. Use this API to onboard an organization, invite teammates, manage fleet assets and operators, open and close assignments, and orchestrate day-to-day logistics work.

This is one of the [audience-scoped Nizam APIs](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/overview). It shares the wire-level conventions (RFC 9457 errors, cursor pagination, expand grammar) with every other Nizam audience — see the [API conventions reference](https://docs.nizam.ai/api/conventions) for the canonical description. This page covers what's specific to the Dashboard.

## Audience

This API ships in the **Dashboard SDK** (`@nizam-os/dashboard-sdk` on npm; equivalent packages on PyPI / Maven Central when the language SDK exists). Consumers are:

- **Tenant admins** — set up the organization, invite users, configure billing, manage integrations.
- **Dispatchers** — operate the fleet: open assignments, track operators, manage tasks and orders.
- **Operations staff** — read-mostly visibility into the operational state.
- **Viewers** — read-only access for stakeholders.

Customers, end-buyers, carriers, and the operator-runtime stack each have their own SDK. If your consumer is a driver app or autopilot, use [`@nizam-os/operator-sdk`](https://docs.nizam.ai/operator) instead.

## Authentication

Issued by the **`nizam-dashboard`** Keycloak client. Authorization Code + PKCE flow — see the [Keycloak setup guide](https://docs.nizam.ai/auth/dashboard) for redirect URI configuration.

Every JWT carries:

| Claim | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `azp` | `nizam-dashboard` — identifies this Portal at the server. |
| `sub` | The user's UUID (matches `identity.users.id`). |
| `organization` | The Keycloak Organization the user belongs to, including its UUID. RLS scopes every database query to this id. |
| `realm_access.roles` | Realm-level roles (e.g., `platform_admin` if the user is internal Nizam staff acting through the Dashboard). |
| `resource_access.nizam-dashboard.roles` | Dashboard roles for this user. |

## Roles

Granted via the `nizam-dashboard` client role assignment in Keycloak:

| Role | Capability |
|---|---|
| `admin` | Full Dashboard access. User invites, organization settings, fleet CRUD. |
| `dispatcher` | Operational dispatching — assignments, tasks, route plans. No org settings, no user invites. |
| `staff` | Read-write on operational state; can't reconfigure the organization. |
| `viewer` | Read-only access. |

Endpoint authorization is layered: `@AccessibleTo(Portal.DASHBOARD)` gates the SDK at the audience boundary; `@PreAuthorize("hasAuthority('dashboard:admin')")` gates individual operations within. The [authorization model](https://docs.nizam.ai/auth/rbac) page walks through both layers.

## Surface

The Dashboard API is Nizam's largest surface — every tenant-side feature shows up here.

| Concept | Highlights |
|---|---|
| **Organizations** | `POST /v1/organizations` to create a tenant. `PATCH /v1/organizations/{id}` for slug / category / domain updates. Owner-only delete. |
| **Users & invites** | `POST /v1/users` invites a teammate. `PATCH /v1/users/{id}` updates contact fields (NO status — status changes are platform-staff only). `DELETE /v1/users/{id}` soft-deletes. |
| **Fleet — assets** | `POST /v1/assets` creates a vehicle / drone / robot / container / trailer. Kind-discriminated. |
| **Fleet — operators** | `POST /v1/operators` registers a human driver, an autonomous software agent, or a teleoperated controller. |
| **Fleet — assignments** | `POST /v1/assignments` binds an operator to an asset in a role. `POST /v1/assignments/{id}/close` ends the binding. Reassignment is open-new + close-old; never mutate in place. |

## Multi-tenancy

Every Dashboard request is scoped to the calling user's Organization via Postgres Row-Level Security. Cross-tenant operations don't exist in this SDK; they live on the [Platform Staff API](https://docs.nizam.ai/platform-staff) — a different SDK with stricter audit.

## Status

The Dashboard surface is the most evolved of the Nizam audiences. New endpoints land here first; cross-Portal patterns are validated on the Dashboard before being mirrored to other SDKs.

get.description: Newest-first feed of audited events for the caller's active organization (dashboard; tenant-scoped). Platform staff see across tenants. This is the durable, REST source of truth behind the realtime `/topic/organization.<id>.activity` STOMP stream: on reconnect, a client passes `since=<last_seen>` to catch up missed items, then resumes realtime. Each item's `event_id` correlates with the realtime ActivityFeedItem's `id` for deduplication. Sortable: `created_at` (default `created_at:desc`). Bidirectional opaque cursors via `starting_after` / `ending_before`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return only activity at or after this instant (ISO-8601). Pass the last-seen timestamp to reconcile after a realtime disconnect.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order. Allowed fields: `created_at`. Append `:asc` or `:desc` to each field (direction required, e.g. `created_at:desc`), comma-separated for multi-sort; unknown fields or directions are rejected with `400 validation_failed`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Default 20, maximum 100. Out-of-range values are silently clamped; the response body's `limit` field reflects what was applied.

parameters.name: starting_after
parameters.description: Opaque cursor — return the page starting strictly after this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `ending_before`.

parameters.name: ending_before
parameters.description: Opaque cursor — return the page ending strictly before this entity in the sort order. Mutually exclusive with `starting_after`.

get.description: Without `q`: the org's assets ordered by `created_at` descending (or an explicit `sort`). With `q`: ranked search across name, VIN, code, plate, serial, call sign, make, model and sub-kind — accent-insensitive and language-agnostic (epic #97). Matching is hybrid: whole words and word-prefixes (type-ahead — `pick` finds `Picker Bot 3`) plus substrings and typos (`ick`, or a misspelled `sprintr`, still match). `q` results are ordered by relevance unless `sort` is given, in which case the search narrows the rows and `sort` orders them. Sort by a single column — the allowed fields and direction grammar are enumerated on the `sort` parameter; `status` and `kind` sort by their domain order (status lifecycle, kind grouping), not the stored code or the tenant-relabeled display string. As filters, `status` / `kind` accept comma-separated values and narrow every mode. Pagination is bidirectional (`starting_after` / `ending_before`); cursors are bound to the sort that minted them — switching sorts restarts from the first page. `highlight=true` adds a `<mark>`-wrapped match snippet (relevance mode only).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text search query (max 200 chars).

parameters.name: highlight
parameters.description: Include a highlighted match snippet per hit (search mode only).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle status. Comma-separated; matched case-insensitively.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Filter by top-level kind. Comma-separated; matched case-insensitively.

parameters.description: Only assets created on or after this calendar day (`yyyy-mm-dd`), inclusive — widened server-side to the start of the day in UTC, so the whole day counts.

post.description: Creates a new asset (vehicle, drone, robot, container, equipment, ...) owned by the active organization.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Supply a UUID (canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form; lowercase v4 recommended) to make this operation idempotent: the same key on a retry replays the original outcome instead of creating a second resource. 2xx successes and deliberate 4xx domain rejections are cached and replayed for 24h when the request body matches; transient 5xx responses are never cached, so a retry with the same key re-executes. A malformed key is rejected with 400 `idempotency.invalid_key`; reusing a key with a different request body is 409 `idempotency.key_conflict`; a key still in flight is 409 `idempotency.in_progress`. Omit the header and the operation behaves like any other write.

post.summary: Legal status transitions for a selection
post.description: Returns the lifecycle statuses EVERY asset in the selection may legally move to next — the intersection of each asset's legal-transition set (the same matrix the per-asset `allowed_transitions` field and the transition verbs enforce). The status picker calls this so a bulk change offers only moves legal for the WHOLE selection, instead of offering every status and relying on per-row 409s. Ids that don't resolve to a live asset in your organization are ignored; a selection that shares no common next status (e.g. it includes a terminal sold/lost asset) returns an empty list. It is a read — re-asserting it is free.

200.description: The statuses legal for the whole selection.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Supply a UUID (canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form; lowercase v4 recommended) to make this operation idempotent: the same key on a retry replays the original outcome instead of creating a second resource. 2xx successes and deliberate 4xx domain rejections are cached and replayed for 24h when the request body matches; transient 5xx responses are never cached, so a retry with the same key re-executes. A malformed key is rejected with 400 `idempotency.invalid_key`; reusing a key with a different request body is 409 `idempotency.key_conflict`; a key still in flight is 409 `idempotency.in_progress`. Omit the header and the operation behaves like any other write.

organization the caller is currently an active member of — otherwise the call fails
with `403 tenant.not_a_member` (same code the X-Nizam-Organization header path uses),
never silently writes the preference for an inaccessible org.

On success, returns the new bundled state in one round-trip. The cached
membership context for the caller is invalidated so the next request sees the new
preference immediately.

post.description: Builds a draft settlement statement for a merchant: pulls the merchant's reconcilable COD collections into source lines and reconciles them, appends any manual fee / adjustment lines, and foots gross/fees/net. 422 `billing_party.unknown` if the `merchant_id` does not belong to the organization; 409 `merchant_payout.period_already_settled` if a live payout already covers the same merchant + period; 422 `merchant_payout.currency_mismatch` on a mixed-currency line.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. Supply a UUID (canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form; lowercase v4 recommended) to make this operation idempotent: the same key on a retry replays the original outcome instead of creating a second resource. 2xx successes and deliberate 4xx domain rejections are cached and replayed for 24h when the request body matches; transient 5xx responses are never cached, so a retry with the same key re-executes. A malformed key is rejected with 400 `idempotency.invalid_key`; reusing a key with a different request body is 409 `idempotency.key_conflict`; a key still in flight is 409 `idempotency.in_progress`. Omit the header and the operation behaves like any other write.
